context.verdict: The resume scores 70 out of 100. Rule 1 earned full points (20) because more than 15 relevant technical keywords appear in context. Rule 2 received 5 points as the candidate only lists a vague student title rather than a clear professional title. Rule 3 got 7 points for having three of the four standard headings (Education, Projects, Skills) but missing an Experience section. Rule 4 earned full marks (5) – the text parses cleanly with no multi‑column artifacts. Rule 5 received the maximum 15 points for a well‑organized Skills section with over ten items across categories. Rule 6 got 0 points because no bullet includes quantified results. Rule 7 earned 10 points for a complete education entry; the listed certifications are gamified badges and therefore did not add extra credit. Rule 8 got full credit (5) – no graphics or icons detected. Rule 9 lost points (2) due to mixed date formats (year‑only vs month‑year). Rule 10 earned 5 points as all four contact elements are present and placed in the main body. Rule 11 received 5 points for an appropriate length (≈400 words). However, because the resume lacks any formal work experience, the Critical Calibration Rule caps the final score at 70.
